headline: The EST, ACME, and CMP clients reach a CA through a forward HTTP proxy, with the same opts.proxy the SCEP client already accepts.
summary: pki.est, pki.acme.client, and pki.cmp.transfer now accept opts.proxy = { url, auth?, tls? } and reach the CA through a forward HTTP proxy over the shared transport, joining pki.scep. A CONNECT tunnel is opened to the proxy and the origin TLS is negotiated inside it under the identical origin trust policy, so the proxy carries the enrollment without being able to read it or substitute the origin certificate. Basic proxy authentication (RFC 7617) is sent only over an https:// proxy, whose own certificate is verified against proxy.tls; an http:// proxy is tunnel-only and carrying auth on one is refused (proxy-auth-requires-tls). The proxy option is validated and enforced entirely by the transport, so every client inherits the identical checks; a malformed option, a failed CONNECT, an unverified proxy certificate, or an unaccepted credential fails closed. Proxied revocation fetching and CT-log retrieval remain a separate future increment.

Added: pki.est.cacerts / simpleenroll / simplereenroll / serverkeygen / csrattrs / fullcmc, pki.acme.client, and pki.cmp.transfer accept opts.proxy = { url, auth?, tls? } to reach the CA through a forward HTTP proxy, the same option pki.scep accepts. The origin TLS is negotiated inside the proxy's CONNECT tunnel under the identical origin trust policy; Basic authentication (RFC 7617) is sent only over an https:// proxy verified against proxy.tls, and an http:// proxy is tunnel-only. The option is deep-copied at the call so a later change to the caller's object cannot alter the proxy in use.
